ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The authoritative command is something the records enact, raises, or demands in force, commonly in military and public-command language.
EvidenceBody: The authoritative command currently being carried out or brought fully into effect. The term occurs 1,503 times in 291 allowlisted texts. Chan records place this governmental and military command language on the public teaching seat: a questioner asks what Fenyang Shanzhao will show ‘when the command is carried out’; Longtan Yuan declares that ‘the command has already been carried out’; Rui'an Sengyin associates Yunmen Wenyan's command with blows that distinguish dragons from snakes; and Baichi Yuan describes Baoshou as commanding within the realm and holding authority beyond the gate. Stock forms include ‘the command is put into effect’ ( in ), ‘fully bring forward the command’ (170 in 103), and ‘the command has already been carried out’ (28 in 23). Chengtian Que also criticizes even ‘raising the command's guiding principle’ as making an artificial nest, showing that criticism and exercise can take the same command as their object.
